Unfortunately due to the nature of Time Gating and rapid wipe cycles (6 Week Per Server) I cannot recommend the game. The amount of content available on a per week basis is far too light to promote long term play, and the content unlocked on subsequent weeks doesn't add enough to keep a healthy gameplay flow.

On top of this the Cosmetics you unlock, the blueprints you gain, and any real money purchases you choose to make will be locked per character, as nothing is "Account Bound"
You cannot delete a character and you cannot transfer a character to a different world either.

Addition: With Phase 3 Hard prime wars are introduced, with a heavy restriction that is not made clear to the player about obtaining "Frontier Pass", In order to obtain the pass you must get 1000 Score in other Prime Wars, The only surefire way to get that score is... Build a bunch of small wooden fences in a circle (Addition to this: As of now people spam the missiles before anybody else has a chance to contribute so only a few people pass this threshold)

Getting into it 
It’s a strange game at first, but once it clicks there’s a lot of fun here. I’ve put in around 254 hours and even after taking a break, I know I’ll return. It has that “one more thing to do” feeling with building, exploring and upgrading.

Style and world 
It’s clearly an Asian-made game and the aesthetics are great. Outfits, weapons and fashion actually look cool, which is something a lot of Western games forget. The world design is weird in a good way, with creatures, biomes and bosses that feel memorable.

Servers and progression 
Each server is its own world with a story and time-gated progress. Join a fresh one if you can, older worlds get quiet near the end. The beginner world is easy but doesn’t have everything unlocked. Once you understand this system, it makes more sense and gives you clear goals to work toward.

Gameplay mix 
You get a bit of everything: shooting, crafting, collecting creatures, dungeons, base-building and exploring. Building is surprisingly fun and some players make insane designs. Bikes and cars make travelling feel fast and satisfying. There’s also a permanent world where all your progress carries over between seasons.

Quick notes 
Combat can be a little simple at times and some systems can feel messy until you learn them, but overall it stays engaging if you like upgrading, looting and creating your own base.

“Staring at the stars and I keep finding more
Breaking through the darkness shining brighter than before
You're the northern lights I keep on chasing
You're an ever-changing wonder to explore

Oh my heart is aching but I finally found a cure
If you're a breaking wave maybe I could be the shore”

These lyrics perfectly capture the vibe of the game. The game itself gives you a nostalgic feeling even while you’re playing — like a déjà vu dream you keep coming back to. The visuals are stunninggg and make the whole world feel like a strange but beautiful dreamscape.

And honestly… who here has fallen asleep and ended up dreaming about being in this game? Because I have. My friends have too. It just sticks with you, like “kabiyak ng ating gunita” kind of way.
